title: S1 and S9 Source Gap Reconciliation

historical_gap_reconciliation.notes: Later S1 source adds an explicit order-of-precedence rule and formal escalation requirement. Migration still requires curator review of wording before canonical promotion.
Later S1 source states that availability does not grant reliance and delegates detailed suitability/reliance rules to information-requirement and validation/delivery standards.

S1 intentionally declares authority principles without enumerating all assignments. The dedicated role registry/definitions now provide the operational role layer. A future machine-checkable RACI/function/authority matrix may still improve completeness but is not required to make S1 internally complete.

historical_gap_reconciliation.topic: Information reliability, suitability and permitted reliance
historical_gap_reconciliation.notes: S1 declares the principle and explicitly delegates detailed reliability/suitability/LOD-LOI/reliance rules. These downstream domains are substantially present in the migration branch.

historical_gap_reconciliation.topic: Required versus optional model uses by phase and stakeholder
historical_gap_reconciliation.notes: No dedicated governed model-use taxonomy was identified in the current repository or the reviewed S1 source set. Do not invent one during migration.

repository_architecture_conflict.notes: The Confluence layer-governance source uses a legacy L1-L7 model in which L1 is the constitution and L7 is validation/evidence. The GitHub repository already adopted a different governed layer model: L1 external authority, L2 doctrine, L3 architecture, L4 standards, L5 workflows, L6 instructions, L7 configurations. Source concepts should be preserved but remapped to the repository layer architecture rather than copied literally.

S1.recommended_next_migration_object: S1 parent constitutional/doctrine object plus references to existing role and downstream standards; no new role enumeration inside S1.

gap_reconciliation.notes: A detailed governance scaffold exists, but it explicitly contains no real automation entries. The source defines expected fields and production rules; a concrete registry must be created only through curator action.
A detailed conceptual schema and governance scaffold exists, but it explicitly contains no concrete tool/domain rows.

existing_repository_support.notes: Defines approval/responsibility for tools and automation and references a future S9 parent. It does not replace the missing S9 standard or the concrete registries.
S3, S5, S6, S7 and the Revit/interoperability extraction already contain rules that consume tool/automation authority. These should reference S9 once the parent is migrated.

S9.recommended_next_migration_object: Migrate the S9 parent standard first. Keep Automation Registry and Tool Authority Matrix as explicitly unresolved governed assets until curator-approved concrete content exists.

curator_boundary: Do not create concrete automation entries from examples, scripts or products merely because the scaffold defines fields.
Do not populate a Tool Authority Matrix by inference from common industry practice; only source-supported or explicitly curated assignments may become governed rows.
Do not reproduce the legacy source layer numbering as canonical GitHub architecture where it conflicts with the repository's accepted layer model.

provenance.migration_note: Gap reconciliation only; no canonical S1 or S9 content promoted by this file.
